question: In a single-slit diffraction experiment, the slit width is doubled while the wavelength remains the same. What happens to the angular width of the central maximum? Give reason.

options.A: The angular width of the central maximum doubles because it is proportional to slit width.
options.B: The angular width remains unchanged because wavelength is unchanged.
options.C: The central angular width is $\dfrac{2\lambda}{a}$. If slit width changes from $a$ to $2a$, the new width is $\dfrac{2\lambda}{2a}=\dfrac{\lambda}{a}$, which is half the original width.
options.D: The angular width becomes one-fourth because it varies as $1/a^2$.
